STORY SO FAR: Thu 08-06, a short afternoon session and the biggest close of the week. THE -OM SLIP IS DEAD. I paid off the morning trailer with a real ambush — atthai at the door, 'saaptingala?', nothing in the prompt about who ate — and he fired 'ama saapittom' cold, first ask, unaided. Second novel slot in a fresh scene ('enga poneenga?' at the gate) came back 'market-ku ponom', which is the exact wrong answer he gave on Tuesday, now right. 1pl-past-om (8x over 10d) and it-tail-uchu both CLOSED. frame:we-om is cold, engines 19/21, survival 28/34. The lesson for me: it did not close in chat. It closed because M82 sat in his ear on a walk and then I stopped helping. Twice now the audio has done what my teaching could not - when a slip escalates, change the lane, do not re-teach harder.

THE FIELD MISSION LANDED: bare 'paravaayilla' deployed live to an apology, one day after being taught. Shortest word-to-real-room gap this system has had, and it validates last night's standing rule (teach it before you assign it, give it a real audience).

NEW SLIP, AND IT IS THE INTERESTING ONE: catch-closing. Ran a five-line verandah gossip tape at native speed (Vasanth borrowed from amma, cannot repay). He took the propositional content clean off a verb he does not own (vaangittaan) and pulled '-aam' as 'I heard' unprompted - that decoder is genuinely solid. But he stopped at 'alaichal jaasti = too many problems' and never reported the last two lines, which are where the exchange actually resolves: 'summa solraanga' is the second cousin KILLING the story, and 'seri seri, vittudu' is the topic being shut down. Pair this with 08-05 (read akka's 'nee solradhu puriyudhu' as confusion when it was surrender): he decodes the MIDDLE of an exchange and misses WHERE IT LANDS. That is the catch axis's real shape - not speed, not coverage, but the closing stance. Commissioned as a phone_call dose (one side of three calls, three different endings) because a phone call's ending is unmissable.

I ALSO BROKE THE SURFACE RULE - put Tamil script in chat twice and he called it. Chat is phonetic, always. He also asked what 'sollu' said and confused it with 'seri'; taught the pair (sollu = the demand, seri = the shrug).

NUMBERS I OWE A CORRECTION ON: I told him catch went to 4/12. It did not - frame:hearsay-aam was already solid, catch is still 3/12. Correct it at the next open.

TONIGHT'S MISSION: first time she asks about anything the two of them did today, answer in Tamil with the -om tail (ponom / saapittom), organic slot, no setup. Collect tomorrow.

STILL OPEN, never slotted: puriyala-for-reopen (he owns the word's shape, not its conversational job). Volley frozen at 2/4 (KF-14). One ask per message is the house rule. Boot overhead is still visible to him - open fast, no ceremony.

soak_order.focus: the CLOSE of an exchange, never its middle. Every scene must END on a stance and the ending must be audible: சும்மா சொல்றாங்க killing a story dead, விட்டுடு dropping it, சரி சரி conceding. Permute the same gossip across three calls with three different landings — the win is not what happened, it is which way it landed and who ended it. Production demanded: zero.
